$doc: SINGLE SOURCE for RUN's rareKills crowd allow-list (WP-B / RUN-E). Edit THIS file, then run `python pipeline/gen_crowd_schema.py` to regenerate the mirrors: RUN/data/generated/crowd_schema.lua (addon payload builder), firebase/rareKills.rules.partial (the validRareKill server gate, applied verbatim into the Foresight repo web/firestore.rules between the same markers), and ../marketing/web/run-crowd-schema.js (web sanitize for run.html). The drift check (`gen_crowd_schema.py --check`) fails if any committed mirror differs, so a new field can never land in one consumer and leak past another. DATA-MINIMIZATION LAW: this is an ALLOW-LIST of non-identifying game data. The payload is an envelope { v, kinds, events, season, clientId?, sum?, named?, handle?, armory? }; each events[] element is one of the event shapes under 'events' (rules cannot iterate lists, so event internals are deep-validated by the addon builder, the web sanitize, and the rareKillsOnWrite function). 'identifying' fields ship ONLY under the opt-in named==true tier (a chosen handle, never a real name). 'nm' on sightings is a CREATURE name (game data), never a player's.

fields.doc: distinct event kinds present in events[]
season tag (s0 until the Hardcore-kickoff reset)
Fletcher16 over the canonical event string (tamper/truncation tell)
opt-in: show me on Giant Slayers; GATES handle/armory
chosen handle (never a real name); only when named==true
optional armory URL (https only, charset-locked); only when named==true
player level floored to 10s - coarse, non-identifying

slay.doc: a solo-wager win (RISK IT); the server RECOMPUTES the tier from snap and ignores p

fields.doc: recomputable odds inputs at arm time; without it the server cannot verify and skips the entry

sighting.doc: a rare+ creature actually seen; names publish only at k-of-n distinct reporters

fields.doc: CREATURE name as the client saw it (game data, never a player name)

wipe.doc: a group wipe; exactly one of npc (open world) or enc (boss encounter name)

calib.doc: consent-gated odds-calibration pair (RUN-P): the predicted solo win chance vs what actually happened; pl/cl/cls are the recomputable odds inputs (the slay-snap precedent) and the server recomputes p, treating the client's as advisory

fields.doc: player level at assess time (exact - the odds input, as slay.snap.pLevel)
client-predicted win %, ADVISORY only - the server recomputes from pl/cl/cls
